summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a right tunneled femoral catheter, HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and recent MRSA bacteremia on IV vancomycin presented with profuse diarrhea from Clostridium difficile colitis and palpitations. In the ED she was found to be in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (rates up to ~150) felt precipitated by infection and dehydration; after IV fluids and initiation of oral vancomycin she converted to normal sinus rhythm and remained stable without need for chronic rate-control therapy. Her severe C. difficile colitis improved with decreasing stool frequency, benign abdominal exams, and normal lactate; she was discharged to extended care with oral vancomycin to continue for a prolonged course (extending two weeks beyond completion of IV vancomycin). She continued IV vancomycin dosed with hemodialysis for MRSA bacteremia, received hemodialysis on the day of discharge, and was counseled to hold stool softeners during diarrhea. Subtherapeutic INR on chronic warfarin (for clotting risk/history) was noted with a plan for repeat INR in ~3 days and outpatient dose adjustment; chronic hypotension was managed with continued midodrine, and reflux symptoms were treated with calcium carbonate while avoiding PPIs/H2 blockers due to interaction with atazanavir.
problems: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (resolved)
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
MRSA bacteremia on IV vancomycin with hemodialysis
HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Subtherapeutic INR/abnormal coagulation profile on long-term warfarin
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications (history)
